correctness.rationale: For every n≥4 the finite orbit-compatibility graph is derived from all four original Hamming distances. Its maximal cliques are supported in coordinate squares; each square induces a join of two circles (a three-sphere), with all pairwise block intersections contained in a common thickened cube-edge graph. That graph deformation retracts to the cube one-skeleton. The circles in sphere-block intersections attach nullhomotopically to their respective three-spheres, so homotopy pushouts add one S³ for each cubical square and fill each perimeter with a two-cell. The simply connected cubical two-skeleton is a wedge of S² with Euler-characteristic rank. The integral result holds in all dimensions. An independent GF(2) clique-boundary computation checks n=4..9 without being treated as the infinite proof.
